- We do not engage in cross-marketing or link-referral programs.
- We do not employ tracking devices for marketing purposes.

- With your consent (e.g. if you authorize us to share data with other users).
- In connection with a merger, bankruptcy, or sale/transfer of assets.

# Live Reloading When building your app it can be useful to view your changes in a web browser as you make them. FastHTML supports live reloading which means that it watches for any changes to your code and automatically refreshes the webpage in your browser. To enable live reloading simply replace [`FastHTML`](https://www.fastht.ml/docs/api/core.html#fasthtml) in your app with `FastHTMLWithLiveReload`. ``` python from fasthtml.common import * app = FastHTMLWithLiveReload() ``` Then in your terminal run `uvicorn` with reloading enabled. uvicorn main:app --reload **⚠️ Gotchas** - A reload is only triggered when you save your changes. - `FastHTMLWithLiveReload` should only be used during development. - If your app spans multiple directories you might need to use the `--reload-dir` flag to watch all files in each directory. See the uvicorn [docs](https://www.uvicorn.org/settings/#development) for more info. - The live reload script is only injected into the page when rendering [ft components](https://www.fastht.ml/docs/explains/explaining_xt_components.html). ## Live reloading with `fast_app` In development the `fast_app` function provides the same functionality. It instantiates the `FastHTMLWithLiveReload` class if you pass `live=True`:
**main.py** ``` python from fasthtml.common import * app, rt = fast_app(live=True) serve() ```
Line 3 `fast_app()` instantiates the `FastHTMLWithLiveReload` class. Line 5 [`serve()`](https://www.fastht.ml/docs/api/core.html#serve) is a wrapper around a `uvicorn` call. To run `main.py` in live reload mode, just do `python main.py`. We recommend turning off live reload when deploying your app to production.

Welcome to the official FastHTML documentation.
FastHTML is a new next-generation web framework for fast, scalable web applications with minimal, compact code. It’s designed to be:
- Powerful and expressive enough to build the most advanced, interactive web apps you can imagine.
- Fast and lightweight, so you can write less code and get more done.
- Easy to learn and use, with a simple, intuitive syntax that makes it easy to build complex apps quickly.
FastHTML apps are just Python code, so you can use FastHTML with the full power of the Python language and ecosystem. FastHTML’s functionality maps 1:1 directly to HTML and HTTP, but allows them to be encapsulated using good software engineering practices—so you’ll need to understand these foundations to use this library fully. To understand how and why this works, please read this first: fastht.ml/about.
Installation
Since fasthtml is a Python library, you can install it with:
pip install python-fasthtml
In the near future, we hope to add component libraries that can likewise be installed via pip.
Usage
For a minimal app, create a file “main.py” as follows:
main.py
from fasthtml.common import *
app,rt = fast_app()
@rt('/')
def get(): return Div(P('Hello World!'), hx_get="/change")
serve()
Running the app with python main.py prints out a link to your running app: http://localhost:5001. Visit that link in your browser and you should see a page with the text “Hello World!”. Congratulations, you’ve just created your first FastHTML app!
Adding interactivity is surprisingly easy, thanks to HTMX. Modify the file to add this function:
main.py
@rt('/change')
def get(): return P('Nice to be here!')
You now have a page with a clickable element that changes the text when clicked. When clicking on this link, the server will respond with an “HTML partial”—that is, just a snippet of HTML which will be inserted into the existing page. In this case, the returned element will replace the original P element (since that’s the default behavior of HTMX) with the new version returned by the second route.
This “hypermedia-based” approach to web development is a powerful way to build web applications.
Getting help from AI
Because FastHTML is newer than most LLMs, AI systems like Cursor, ChatGPT, Claude, and Copilot won’t give useful answers about it. To fix that problem, we’ve provided an LLM-friendly guide that teaches them how to use FastHTML. To use it, add this link for your AI helper to use:
This example is in a format based on recommendations from Anthropic for use with Claude Projects. This works so well that we’ve actually found that Claude can provide even better information than our own documentation! For instance, read through this annotated Claude chat for some great getting-started information, entirely generated from a project using the above text file as context.
If you use Cursor, type @doc then choose “Add new doc”, and use the /llms-ctx.txt link above. The context file is auto-generated from our llms.txt (our proposed standard for providing AI-friendly information)—you can generate alternative versions suitable for other models as needed.
Next Steps
Start with the official sources to learn more about FastHTML:
- About: Learn about the core ideas behind FastHTML
- Documentation: Learn from examples how to write FastHTML code
- Idiomatic app: Heavily commented source code walking through a complete application, including custom authentication, JS library connections, and database use.
We also have a 1-hour intro video:
The capabilities of FastHTML are vast and growing, and not all the features and patterns have been documented yet. Be prepared to invest time into studying and modifying source code, such as the main FastHTML repo’s notebooks and the official FastHTML examples repo:
Then explore the small but growing third-party ecosystem of FastHTML tutorials, notebooks, libraries, and components:
- FastHTML Gallery: Learn from minimal examples of components (ie chat bubbles, click-to-edit, infinite scroll, etc)

# FastHTML

> FastHTML is a python library which brings together Starlette, Uvicorn, HTMX, and fastcore's `FT` "FastTags" into a library for creating server-rendered hypermedia applications. The `FastHTML` class itself inherits from `Starlette`, and adds decorator-based routing with many additions, Beforeware, automatic `FT` to HTML rendering, and much more.

Things to remember when writing FastHTML apps:

- Although parts of its API are inspired by FastAPI, it is *not* compatible with FastAPI syntax and is not targeted at creating API services
- FastHTML includes support for Pico CSS and the fastlite sqlite library, although using both are optional; sqlalchemy can be used directly or via the fastsql library, and any CSS framework can be used. Support for the Surreal and css-scope-inline libraries are also included, but both are optional
- FastHTML is compatible with JS-native web components and any vanilla JS library, but not with React, Vue, or Svelte
- Use `serve()` for running uvicorn (`if __name__ == "__main__"` is not needed since it's automatic)
- When a title is needed with a response, use `Titled`; note that that already wraps children in `Container`, and already includes both the meta title as well as the H1 element.

## Docs

- [FastHTML concise guide](https://www.fastht.ml/docs/ref/concise_guide.html.md): A brief overview of idiomatic FastHTML apps
- [HTMX reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/bigskysoftware/htmx/master/www/content/reference.md): Brief description of all HTMX attributes, CSS classes, headers, events, extensions, js lib methods, and config options
- [Starlette quick guide](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/jph00/e91192e9bdc1640f5421ce3c904f2efb/raw/61a2774912414029edaf1a55b506f0e283b93c46/starlette-quick.md): A quick overview of some Starlette features useful to FastHTML devs.

## API

- [API List](https://www.fastht.ml/docs/apilist.txt): A succint list of all functions and methods in fasthtml.
- [MonsterUI API List](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AnswerDotAI/MonsterUI/refs/heads/main/docs/apilist.txt): Complete API Reference for Monster UI, a component framework similar to shadcn, but for FastHTML


## Examples

- [Websockets application](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AnswerDotAI/fasthtml/main/examples/basic_ws.py): Very brief example of using websockets with HTMX and FastHTML
- [Todo list application](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AnswerDotAI/fasthtml/main/examples/adv_app.py): Detailed walk-thru of a complete CRUD app in FastHTML showing idiomatic use of FastHTML and HTMX patterns.

## Optional

- [Surreal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/AnswerDotAI/surreal/main/README.md): Tiny jQuery alternative for plain Javascript with inline Locality of Behavior, providing `me` and `any` functions
- [Starlette full documentation](https://gist.githubusercontent.com/jph00/809e4a4808d4510be0e3dc9565e9cbd3/raw/9b717589ca44cedc8aaf00b2b8cacef922964c0f/starlette-sml.md): A subset of the Starlette documentation useful for FastHTML development.

- [FastHTML by Example](https://www.fastht.ml/docs/tutorials/by_example.html.md): A collection of 4 FastHTML apps showcasing idiomatic use of FastHTML and HTMX patterns.
- [Using Jupyter to write FastHTML](https://www.fastht.ml/docs/tutorials/jupyter_and_fasthtml.html.md): A guide to developing FastHTML apps inside Jupyter notebooks.
- [FT Components](https://www.fastht.ml/docs/explains/explaining_xt_components.html.md): Explanation of the `FT` components, which are a way to write HTML in a Pythonic way.
- [FAQ](https://www.fastht.ml/docs/explains/faq.html.md): Answers to common questions about FastHTML.
- [MiniDataAPI Spec](https://www.fastht.ml/docs/explains/minidataapi.html.md): Explanation of the MiniDataAPI specification, which allows us to use the same API for many different database engines.
- [OAuth](https://www.fastht.ml/docs/explains/oauth.html.md): Tutorial and explanation of how to use OAuth in FastHTML apps.

# Film Connection

> Film Connection is a film industry apprenticeship (externship) program. Students learn filmmaking, cinematography, editing, and screenwriting one-on-one inside working production companies and studios, mentored by film professionals, instead of attending a traditional film school. Locations across the United States.

Film Connection is part of the Recording Radio Film Connection & CASA Schools family (rrfedu.com). The model: you are placed with a working mentor in a real production environment near where you live, and you learn on actual productions.

- [Ultimate Filmmaking Course](https://filmconnection.com/courses/ultimate-filmmaking-course/): Comprehensive filmmaking program covering directing, producing, and production
- [Cinematography](https://filmconnection.com/courses/cinematography/): Camera, lighting, and visual storytelling taught on real sets
- [Film Production & Editing](https://filmconnection.com/courses/film-production-and-editing/): Hands-on production and post-production training
- [All courses](https://filmconnection.com/courses/)

## Key pages

- [How it works / About us](https://filmconnection.com/about-us/)
- [Meet our mentors](https://filmconnection.com/meet-our-mentors/): The working film professionals who train students
- [Locations](https://filmconnection.com/locations/): Cities where mentors are available
- [Tuition](https://filmconnection.com/film-school-tuition/): Program cost compared with traditional film school
- [Reviews](https://filmconnection.com/reviews/): Student reviews and outcomes
- [Reference library](https://filmconnection.com/reference-library/): Free articles on film careers, techniques, and the industry
- [Resources](https://filmconnection.com/resources/)

## Notes

- Film Connection is an apprenticeship/mentorship program, not a film school; it positions itself as the alternative to film school.
- Sister programs: Recording Connection (audio engineering, recordingconnection.com), Radio Connection (broadcasting, radioconnection.com), CASA Schools (culinary, casaschools.com).

FAQ
What are credits?
Every paid plan includes monthly credits that power Agents, Localization, and other AI features. Credits are shared across your entire workspace and its editors. Running low? Upgrade a site or add an add-on for more.
¹ On the free plan, when your workspace has no active subscriptions, you receive 500 credits to try Agents. Upgrade any of your sites to unlock more.
What’s included in the Free plan?
Projects on the Free plan include access to 10 CMS collections, 1,000 pages, 5 MB file uploads, and one free locale to try. This makes it easy to explore Framer, use it as a design tool, or create templates. To connect a custom domain, you’ll need to upgrade to a paid plan. Workspaces without a subscription also support collaboration with up to three editors.
Which plan is right for me?
How are extra editors billed?
Editors are billed per seat and can be added to your workspace or projects at any time. We will notify you when an editor is added to your billing, and you will be charged within 24 hours.
What happens if I go over a limit?
When you reach certain limits, we will ask you to upgrade your plan in Framer. For other limits, like bandwidth, we allow you to exceed your limit for one month. You’ll receive a notification via email so you can upgrade your plan accordingly.
How many add-ons can you purchase on the Pro plan?
With add-ons you can have up to 40,000 CMS items, 40 CMS collections, 2 TB of bandwidth, 700 pages, and 1.5M events on the Pro plan.
How are events billed for the Convert add-on?
You will be billed based on the number of analytics events your site generates each month. An event can be a page view, a click on a tracked link, or a submission through a tracked form. With the add-on, you can also run up to 5 A/B tests. The add-on is billed as part of the billing cycle for the associated plan.
What’s included in the Advanced Hosting add-on?
With the Advanced Hosting add-on, you can add up to 6 rewrites and set custom values for the Permissions-Policy, Referrer-Policy, and X-Frame-Options headers. You can also upload up to 500 static files.
What if my open-source or side project receives a lot of traffic?
What payment methods do you offer?
You can pay for your Framer subscription with a credit card or, in some regions, via PayPal. Alternatively, we offer custom billing options, including credit cards or bank transfers, for Enterprise plans.
What is your refund policy?
If you live in the EU or Turkey, you are legally eligible for a refund if your subscription was purchased within the last 14 days. To claim your refund, please contact our Support team; they will cancel your subscription and process the refund.

# Framer

> Framer is an AI website builder and visual design platform for designers, marketers, and teams. Create responsive websites on a canvas, manage CMS content, and publish with built-in hosting, SEO, and analytics.

AI and agent changes stay editable on the canvas. For coding assistants working inside a Framer project, start with External Agents and the developer documentation.

Links with ?md request a Markdown view. If that view is unavailable, use the same page without the parameter. Use Pricing for current rates, credit allowances, billing terms, and add-ons.

## Product

- [Homepage](https://www.framer.com/): Overview of Framer’s visual canvas, AI agents, CMS, and website publishing.
- [Pricing](https://www.framer.com/pricing?md): Current plans, billing options, AI credits, editor fees, limits, and add-ons.
- [Design](https://www.framer.com/design/?md): Responsive layouts, visual editing, components, effects, and freeform design work.
- [CMS](https://www.framer.com/cms/?md): Collections, fields, detail pages, content imports, and bulk updates with agents.
- [Hosting](https://www.framer.com/hosting/?md): Custom domains, SSL, security, global delivery, redirects, and advanced hosting options.
- [Publishing](https://www.framer.com/publish/?md): Staging, production deployments, password protection, version history, and rollback.
- [Collaboration](https://www.framer.com/collaborate/?md): Branching, preview links, comments, team roles, and review before publishing.
- [SEO](https://www.framer.com/seo/?md): Page metadata, sitemaps, indexing, structured data, redirects, and SEO audits.
- [Performance](https://www.framer.com/performance/?md): Pre-rendering, image optimization, predictive loading, and page-performance techniques.
- [Analytics](https://www.framer.com/analytics?md): Cookie-free visitor analytics, traffic sources, page reports, and filters.
- [Convert](https://www.framer.com/convert/?md): Conversion funnels, A/B tests, and visitor-triggered experiences through the Convert add-on.

## AI and agents

- [Framer AI](https://www.framer.com/ai/?md): Create and refine sites from prompts, then edit the result on the canvas.
- [Framer Agents](https://www.framer.com/agents/?md): Examples for updating layouts, managing CMS content, building components, and auditing sites.
- [External Agents](https://www.framer.com/agents/external/?md): Connect Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, and other AI tools to a Framer project.
- [Skills](https://www.framer.com/skills?md): Create reusable instructions for design systems, writing, CMS work, and repeated tasks.
- [Make your site readable by AI agents](https://www.framer.com/help/articles/make-site-readable-by-ai-agents/): How Framer serves HTML and Markdown to AI tools, including access through ?md.

## Learning and support

- [Help Center](https://www.framer.com/help/?md): Support articles for site setup, the canvas, CMS, publishing, billing, and troubleshooting.
- [Academy](https://www.framer.com/academy/?md): Lessons on agents, responsive layouts, CMS, publishing, SEO, and design systems.
- [Build your first site](https://www.framer.com/academy/lessons/build-your-first-site?md): Start with a prompt, refine the canvas, check responsive layouts, and publish.
- [Build your CMS](https://www.framer.com/academy/lessons/getting-started-with-the-framer-cms?md): Set up collections and fields, then connect content to detail pages and lists.
- [Connect a custom domain](https://www.framer.com/help/articles/how-to-connect-a-custom-domain/?md): Publish a project and connect a domain or subdomain with the required DNS settings.
- [Localization](https://www.framer.com/help/localization/?md): Guides to locales, translations, language routing, localized content, and right-to-left layouts.
- [Accessibility](https://www.framer.com/help/articles/guide-to-web-accessibility-in-framer/?md): Semantic tags, image alt text, tab order, contrast, and reduced-motion settings.
- [Add an llms.txt file](https://www.framer.com/help/articles/llms-txt-framer/?md): Upload an llms.txt file through Hosting Files and check its published address.

## Developers

- [Developer documentation](https://www.framer.com/developers/?md): Entry points for plugins, React components, overrides, Fetch, and the Server API.
- [Code components](https://www.framer.com/developers/components-introduction?md): Build React components with visual controls for the canvas, previews, and published sites.
- [Code overrides](https://www.framer.com/developers/overrides-introduction?md): Add behavior to existing elements, with guidance on when built-in features are preferable.

What are credits?
Every paid plan includes monthly credits that power Agents, Localization, and other AI features. Credits are shared across your entire workspace and its editors. Running low? Upgrade a site or add an add-on for more.

What’s included in the Free plan?
Projects on the Free plan include access to 10 CMS collections, 1,000 pages, 5 MB file uploads, and one free locale to try. This makes it easy to explore Framer, use it as a design tool, or create templates. To connect a custom domain, you’ll need to upgrade to a paid plan. Workspaces without a subscription also support collaboration with up to three editors.
Which plan is right for me?
How are extra editors billed?
Editors are billed per seat and can be added to your workspace or projects at any time. We will notify you when an editor is added to your billing, and you will be charged within 24 hours.
What happens if I go over a limit?
When you reach certain limits, we will ask you to upgrade your plan in Framer. For other limits, like bandwidth, we allow you to exceed your limit for one month. You’ll receive a notification via email so you can upgrade your plan accordingly.
How many add-ons can you purchase on the Pro plan?
With add-ons you can have up to 40,000 CMS items, 40 CMS collections, 2 TB of bandwidth, 700 pages, and 1.5M events on the Pro plan.

You will be billed based on the number of analytics events your site generates each month. An event can be a page view, a click on a tracked link, or a submission through a tracked form. With the add-on, you can also run up to 5 A/B tests. The add-on is billed as part of the billing cycle for the associated plan.

With the Advanced Hosting add-on, you can add up to 6 rewrites and set custom values for the Permissions-Policy, Referrer-Policy, and X-Frame-Options headers. You can also upload up to 500 static files.
What if my open-source or side project receives a lot of traffic?
What payment methods do you offer?
You can pay for your Framer subscription with a credit card or, in some regions, via PayPal. Alternatively, we offer custom billing options, including credit cards or bank transfers, for Enterprise plans.
What is your refund policy?
If you live in the EU or Turkey, you are legally eligible for a refund if your subscription was purchased within the last 14 days. To claim your refund, please contact our Support team; they will cancel your subscription and process the refund.

observations.title: About Us - Neon Electrical
observations.content:
Why we do what we do
We are a team who enjoy working with our hands and solving problems. There is something deeply satisfying about getting things working exactly as they should.
More than that, we enjoy helping people. We know electrical work can feel overwhelming, especially during renovations or urgent repairs. We love making the process easier, taking the stress out of the job, so people can focus on their home and feel confident about what is happening behind the walls.
The team behind Neon Electrical
We genuinely care about the homes and people we work with. We keep communication clear, turn up when we say we will, and focus on doing the job properly so everything feels straightforward and stress free.
Owner / Director
Josh
Josh Taylor is the owner and director of Neon Electrical. He enjoys staying busy with hands on projects at home, whether that is renovations, gardening, or tinkering away on his classic car. When he is not working, you will often find him outdoors or spending time with his dog Poppy, a lively Blue Heeler who keeps him active and occasionally tags along for electrical jobs!
Administration
Kirsty
Kirsty is a full-time midwife based in Papakura and plays a key role in supporting the business by managing accounts and ensuring all invoicing and payments are kept up to date. Outside of work, Kirsty enjoys getting outdoors for walks and spending quality time with friends and family.
Electrician
John-Henry
John-Henry is a fully qualified electrician with a wide range of industry experience. He has a strong interest and extensive expertise in data and communications, including structured cabling, security cameras, and alarm systems. Outside of work, John-Henry is actively involved in his church community and family life.
Apprentice
Tom
Tom is a first-year electrical apprentice who joined the team after completing work experience with Neon Electrical while still at high school. He has shown strong enthusiasm for the trade and a willingness to learn as he begins his electrical career. Outside of work, Tom is passionate about stock car racing and spends much of his spare time maintaining and preparing his car between race events.
I'm Josh Taylor, owner of Neon Electrical.
After 12 years in the industry, one thing is clear—this job is all about trust.
When you call an electrician, you're inviting someone into your home. You need to be confident that the job will be done right, and with care. When you hire me, you get personal service from someone who treats every detail with the same care and attention I’d expect in my own home.
Life outside work
I'm a family man, married to my amazing wife Kirsty, and I value time spent with family and friends. My Christian faith and my church family at Hills Church are also an important part of my life.
In my spare time, I enjoy working on projects — from home renovations and gardening to restoring my classic car. I love keeping busy and getting stuck into hands-on work.
Meet Poppy, my Blue Heeler apprentice
This is Poppy, my Blue Heeler. She’s full of energy, always up for an adventure, and keeps me on my toes. Whether she’s running alongside me on the weekend or just keeping me company after a long day, Poppy is a big part of my life—and if you’re lucky, she might even make an appearance on a job site!

observations.content:
The Lightroom Plugin allows you to upload your photos and videos directly from Lightroom Classic to Picflow. Keep your work in sync by managing your media inside Lightroom and simply Publish any updates to Picflow.
1. Download & Preparation
Download the latest version of the plugin and move the "Picflow.lrplugin" file to a safe location. We recommend saving it somewhere close to your Lightroom Catalog.
2. Installing the Plug-in
To install the plugin we need to launch the Plug-in Manager. To do this, open Lightroom Classic and then select "File → Plug-in Manager...".
Click "Add" on the bottom left of the Plug-in Manager and select the "Picflow.lrplugin" file in the location you saved it. Click "Done" to complete the installation.
3. Plug-in Setup & Connection
In your Lightroom Classic Library, there should be a new Publish Service called "Picflow". Click the "Set Up..." button to open the Publishing Manager.
In the Publishing Manager, click the "Authorize" button. This will open your browser and ask you to log in to Picflow, if you're not logged in already.
Select the workspace you want to connect and click "Connect Lightroom". You will be taken back to Lightroom. Press "Ok" in the popup to confirm the connection. Finally, press "Save" to finish the setup and close the Publishing Manager.
4. You're Done!
The Lightroom Plug-in is now successfully installed and you can create galleries within Lightroom and upload your media to Picflow. To learn more about this, visit:
Updating the Lightroom Plugin
We regularly release new versions of the plugin to improve reliability, fix bugs, and add new features. Please make sure you use the latest version:
- Replace the old "Picflow.lrplugin" file with the new one.
- Restart Lightroom Classic.
Plugin Settings
You can always update the plug-in settings by right-clicking on the Picflow Publish Services and choose "Edit Settings". There are a couple of settings that you can configure in the Lightroom Plugin:
- File Settings 
Define the output quality or limit the maximum file size.
- Image Sizing 
Choose from various resizing options before exporting images to Picflow.
- Output Sharpening 
You can enable sharpening options on your images.
- Metadata 
Include or exclude certain metadata before exporting to Picflow.
Multi-Workspace Setup
The Lightroom Plugin supports connections to multiple Picflow workspaces. To connect to a new workspace, simply "Right-Click" on an existing Picflow connection and then choose "Create Another Publish Service via "Picflow"...". You then have to go through the authorization steps again, where you can choose your new workspace.
Questions or suggestions? Get in touch!

# Picflow

> Picflow is a modern client gallery and collaboration platform for photographers and creative teams to share, proof, and deliver images and videos. Create branded galleries, collect precise feedback, track approvals, and manage reviews end-to-end.

## Key Features
- Best online proofing platform for professional photographers and creative professionals.
- Boost the approval process and save time with streamlined feedback and real-time notifications.
- Advanced gallery designer with themes, presets and unlimited design options.
- Upload any type of creative assets, including video, RAW photos, PDF, audio, and more.
- Embed online galleries directly on any website with native HTML embeds.
- Loved by customers for its modern design and user experience.
- Digital Asset Management (DAM) platform optimized for simplicity.

## Resources

- [Pricing](https://picflow.com/pricing): Detailed pricing plans and options.
- [Reviews](https://picflow.com/love): Testimonials and feedback from Picflow users.
- [Customers](https://picflow.com/): Case studies and success stories.
- [Blog](https://picflow.com/blog): Articles on creative workflows, online proofing, and digital asset management.
- [Book a Demo](https://meet.picflow.com/demo): Schedule a live demonstration of Picflow.

## Apps and Integrations

- [iPhone App](https://apps.apple.com/app/picflow/id6741537409): Get the Picflow mobile app for iOS.
- [Android App](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.picflow.pwa.twa): Get the Picflow mobile app for Android.
- [Lightroom Plugin](https://help.picflow.com/en/articles/8587606-how-to-install-the-lightroom-plugin): Upload photos and videos directly from Lightroom to Picflow.
- [Zapier](https://zapier.com/apps/picflow/integrations): Automate workflows by connecting Picflow with other apps.
- [Chrome Extension](https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/save-to-picflow/fdengbikckdhbbliklkdnbglacleeogg): Collect assets from all over the web and save them to Picflow.
- Google Drive: Seamless integration with Google Drive for asset storage.
- Dropbox: Add assets from your Dropbox to Picflow.
- Box: Upload assets from your Box account.


## Comparison with Alternatives

- [Picflow vs. Pixieset](https://picflow.com/compare/pixieset-alternative): Picflow is collaboration-first (comments, on-image annotations, approval statuses) for fast client reviews. Pixieset is sales-first with a built-in store and photographer websites.
- [Picflow vs. SmugMug](https://picflow.com/compare/smugmug-alternative): Picflow focuses on proofing and delivery for creative teams. SmugMug centers on portfolio hosting and e-commerce/print sales.

- [Picflow vs. Filestage](https://picflow.com/compare/filestage-alternative): Picflow is a lightweight, client-friendly proofing gallery. Filestage is more complex and less intuitive with staged workflows.
- [Picflow vs. Ziflow](https://picflow.com/compare/ziflow-alternative): Picflow simplifies reviews in branded galleries; Ziflow targets approval for governance and compliance.
- [Picflow vs. Air.inc](https://picflow.com/compare/air-inc-alternative): Picflow is for sharing, proofing, and delivering assets to clients. Air is a more technical DAM-style for managing assets in campaigns.
